correctness.rationale: In the frozen proof the small-gain replacement strictly improves the slow factor but may leave the maximum norm unchanged; that observation alone does not exclude a minimizer. The delivered RESULT closes the gap: any tⱼ<1/(2d) implies R≥∏(1−μtⱼ)>ρ^(r−1)(1−h)>Bᵣ, because all the other slow factors are at least ρ>0. For remaining gains set bⱼ=2dtⱼ−1 in [0,1]. The exact pair-compression identity fixes B=∏bⱼ and lowers the positive slow-mode product, strictly if two b's are below one. The maximum of the increasing 2d-endpoint magnitude B and the decreasing compressed slow-mode bound has its unique minimum at Bᵣ. For the candidate schedule all interior eigenvalues lie in [μ,2d−μ], so full rounds contribute at most ρ^(r−1); a nonnegative correction factor is at most its μ-value and a negative one has magnitude at most Bᵣ. This gives global attainment and, by the strict lower bounds, a unique gain multiset. The one-round intersection and the asymptotic root limit follow directly. The proof covers the stated graph class and does not infer it from the frozen finite-grid checks.
correctness.repair: repairs/2/RESULT.md replaces the small-gain argument by a strict bound on R and states the stationary comparison and related scopes explicitly. The claim and exact checker are otherwise unchanged.

broader_coverage.reasoning: More general allowable kernels, without the same objective and exact sequence constraint, do not optimize the stated scalar schedules. Full-interval bounds over spectra that need not have a bipartite reflection gap do not imply the graph-sharp answer.

evidence: The arbitrary-stage sandwich uses a slow-mode lower bound but does not balance the exact slow-mode product with the 2d-eigenmode multiplier. Two-stage laws constrain a pair, not all r factors.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new ingredient for this claim is holding the product B fixed while compressing all gains with a strict inequality, and then proving attainability on the remaining reflected eigenmodes. A two-stage optimum does not supply these equality and interior-spectrum facts for arbitrary r.

originality.rationale: The supported contribution is the exact all-r≥3 factor and unique admissible multiset under one shared Laplacian and stagewise nonnegativity. The published interval-robust Richardson record has a sharp two-stage law and nonsharp arbitrary-stage bounds. A same-day odd-cycle theorem does not satisfy bipartiteness or the horizon, and the overlapping indexed bipartite exact law is only two-round. The inspected primary filters, reachability and stationary-mixing works ask different optimization questions.
residual_risks: An exact root-constrained filtering or nonstationary Richardson result using other terminology could cover arbitrary r. The targeted literature lookup did not produce decisive evidence beyond the inspected sources.

value.rationale: Stagewise stochasticity is a substantive restriction: it preserves averages and nonnegative probability weights at every intermediate round. At any fixed horizon the theorem replaces a genuine multi-round nonsmooth minimax by an implementable unique schedule and factor depending only on degree and gap. It also proves strict improvement over repeating the optimal single-round scalar gain. These conclusions are useful across the natural bipartite regular network class, not merely a sample calculation or asymptotic bound.
